about.title: Indio Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Indio's streets carry a mix of neighborhood traffic, commuters and travelers passing through on Rt 111. In 2025, public records show 201 injury collisions inside the city, with 266 people injured and 5 lives lost. Monroe Street, Indio Boulevard, Jackson Street and Rt 111 account for a large share of those reports, and crash counts tend to cluster on Tuesday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m. Behind every one of those numbers is someone dealing with pain, missed work and phone calls from an insurer they didn't choose. That's where LawProactive comes in. We aren't a law firm. We're a free service that matches you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Riverside County car accident claims on contingency, so nothing comes out of your pocket unless there is a recovery. California gives you two years to file in most cases, but evidence fades far sooner. Photos, dashcam footage, witness contacts and medical records matter, and reaching out early helps protect them.

whyChoose.title: Why Indio Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines here are shorter than people expect
items.desc: California allows two years to file most car accident claims, but if a city, county or state vehicle was involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. An attorney can pin down which clock applies to your crash.

items.title: Being partly at fault doesn't shut you out
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you shared some blame; your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage. Insurers sometimes overstate your share, which is exactly what a lawyer pushes back on.

items.title: Your pain counts, and it isn't capped
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages in ordinary car accident cases, so your pain, sleepless nights and lost routines are part of the claim. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling me. Should I give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's usually wise to politely decline until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shrink or deny your claim, even when you're just being honest. You can share basic contact and policy information without agreeing to a recorded interview.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Indio Boulevard and the police report is still pending. Can I start a claim anyway?
items.answer: Yes. You don't need the final report in hand to begin, and waiting can cost you evidence like nearby camera footage or witness memories. Save your photos, keep every medical receipt, and note the businesses near the crash site. An attorney can request the report from the responding agency and build the file while it's processed.

items.question: What does it cost to use LawProactive and then hire an attorney?
items.answer: LawProactive is free; we simply connect you with an independent personal injury attorney serving Indio and Riverside County. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means their fee comes out of any recovery rather than your savings. If there's no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.
